stories.title: Tencent launches Hy4, claims China's top tier of open models, but outside benchmark ranks it 13th of 33

articles.title: 텐센트, 'Hy4'로 중국 AI 최상위권 진입 선언…사이버 공격 학습 제한

also_covered_by_unread: Nikkei Asia: Tencent says its Hy4 joins 'top-tier' of open-source AI models
SCMP: Tencent launches Hy4 in bid to break into AI's top tier of open-weight models

facts.fact: Tencent released Hy4 on Nov 4 (local time), the follow-up to the Hy4 Preview from August, with scaled-up pre- and post-training.
Hy4 is a mixture-of-experts model with 770 billion parameters in total, about 49 billion active at inference, and a context window of up to 1 million tokens.
It adds image understanding for the first time and computer-use skills covering both command line and graphical interfaces.
Tencent says it trained on defensive security data (finding and fixing software flaws) and left out attack material, to reduce misuse in cyberattacks.
Final-model weights are not yet released; Tencent plans to publish them with a system card soon, plus a lighter Hy4 Flash model.
On a 579-task finance benchmark judged by 213 finance experts, Hy4 scored 3.04 versus DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 2.97 and Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3 at 2.68 each.
Vals AI's Nov 4 evaluation put Hy4 at 59.35% overall accuracy, 13th of 33 models and 4th among open-weight models, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro (62.52%), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (61.26%) and GLM-5.3 (59.73%).
Tencent itself admits a notable gap to top closed models in research-level math, long coding tasks, self-improvement and advanced visual Q&A.
Hy4 is available on Tencent Cloud, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy and Yuanbao; WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy give some free usage until the 15th.

stories.title: OpenAI Images 2.6 brings animated GIFs to ChatGPT; 4 billion images a week

articles.title: ChatGPT can now make animated GIFs with OpenAI's Images 2.6
오픈AI, '이미지스 2.6' 공개…챗GPT서 움직이는 GIF 생성 지원

facts.fact: OpenAI is adding animated GIFs to ChatGPT with a new image model, Images 2.6; users can make a GIF from a text prompt or an uploaded photo.
Users can change playback speed, look at and edit single frames, and share the GIF.
Images 2.6 is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop and mobile.
Developers get two API models: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare (speed) and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst (quality).
OpenAI says people now make more than 4 billion images a week across ChatGPT and the API, up from 3 billion in September (OpenAI's own figure, covers all image use).
The feature comes months after OpenAI shut down Sora, its AI video app, in March.
OpenAI says image generation is 50% faster and editing precision improved; the GIF feature is rolling out gradually so some accounts do not have it yet.
A new 'Complexity' setting controls how much planning the model does before generating an image.

stories.title: Apple cuts engineers' daily AI spending caps from $300 to $200, more cuts planned

articles.title: Apple cuts engineers' daily AI budgets as it reins in spending
Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage

facts.fact: Per Bloomberg, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for some engineering teams from $300 to $200 in October.
More cuts are planned that could take some engineering teams to $100 a day.
Many staff outside engineering already have a $100 daily cap; Apple has considered $25 for some teams.
Staff can use Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini; some teams are told to switch to cheaper or on-device models.
John Ternus became CEO on 1 September and has pushed Apple to be leaner; Apple cut over 200 jobs in August.
Apple's R&D costs rose 32% in fiscal 2026 on higher infrastructure and AI costs; operating expenses rose 22% to $75.5B.
Other firms cap AI use too: Tesla $200 a week, Uber $1,500 a month per coding tool, Accenture $29 a month on Claude.
TechCrunch notes a 'tokenmaxxing' push earlier this year faded as token bills came due; Apple has been asked for comment.

stories.title: Saudi Aramco takes 49% of state-backed AI company Humain for about $2.6B

articles.title: Saudi Aramco übernimmt knapp die Hälfte des KI-Unternehmens Humain

facts.fact: State-controlled oil company Saudi Aramco took a 49% stake in Saudi AI company Humain.
Aramco contributes about $2.6 billion plus existing AI, computing infrastructure and digital assets; the value of those assets is not given.
Saudi sovereign wealth fund PIF keeps the other 51%.
Humain plans data centers with 3 gigawatts of electrical capacity by 2030.
Humain CEO Tareq Amin told Semafor in September the industry budgets $11-12 million per megawatt, which would imply $33-36 billion for 3 GW (heise's extrapolation; Amin gave no budget).
Aramco also hopes to benefit as an energy supplier to data centers and to commercialize its AI technology.

stories.title: US midterms: voter anger at data centers becomes a political force
stories.region: US (Korea market angle: Korea Times/ZDNet Korea/Seoul shares fell, unread)

articles.title: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming

also_covered_by_unread: Reuters: AI data-center stocks slide after Democratic sweep
Yonhap: Seoul shares sharply down as US midterm results spark AI woes
Korea Times: Democrats' win could compound pressures on AI spending, Korean chipmakers

facts.fact: The Nov 3 midterm results gave Democrats full control of Congress, with Republicans in the White House.
An NBC exit poll: more than half of respondents think AI will do more harm than good; almost 80% oppose data centers in their neighborhood.
Almost 60% said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote.
In Ohio, the county where Meta planned a 700,000-square-foot facility passed a data center ban; OpenAI has eyed a $500 billion data center there backed by over $100 billion in Nvidia financing.
Candidates in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Georgia and South Carolina won after taking a stance against rapid buildout.
Goldman Sachs predicts data center construction delays in states like Georgia and Texas; Morgan Stanley sees Ohio governor-elect Amy Acton as a risk to buildout.
Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez introduced a bill for a nationwide moratorium on new data centers; it could face a veto.
Pro-AI super PACs spent millions in the midterms.

stories.title: KT and Samsung use AI to cut high-speed rail signal drops by about 29%

articles.title: KT·삼성전자, 시속 250km 고속철 '통신 끊김' AI로 잡는다

facts.fact: KT (Korean telecom) and Samsung Electronics cut connection drops on a high-speed rail line by about 29% using AI to tune the wireless network.
At 250 km/h or more, trains switch base stations (handover) often; late handovers cause delays and poor call quality.
AI analyzed signal strength and connection-failure history; delayed connection to the next base station was the main cause of drops.
They adjusted handover timing so switching happens earlier on problem sections.
The trial ran on the Gyeongbu Line between Pyeongtaek (Godeok-myeon) and Hwaseong (Maesong-myeon), announced Nov 5.
Last December the pair validated AI-RAN personalized optimization on a commercial network in Seongnam with about 18,000 subscribers.
KT is considering real-world rollout on high-speed rail.

stories.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor; OpenAI buys Pierre Computer (AI coding tooling land-grab)

articles.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
OpenAI wird mit Übernahme von Pierre Computer zum GitHub-Konkurrenten

facts.fact: Meta acquired Conductor, an AI coding startup that lets users run multiple agents in parallel workspaces; Meta confirmed but gave no details or price.
Conductor was founded in 2024 and launched its core product last summer; its agents come from labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.
Conductor's cloud service shuts down on November 20, after which user cloud data will be deleted.
Meta's Muse agents recently passed 10 million users; Meta launched its own coding agent Muse Code in August.
OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer, a US startup founded in 2023 that builds open-source dev tools and git infrastructure; some are already inside Codex.
heise frames it as OpenAI building a GitHub competitor; Microsoft bought GitHub in 2018 for $7.5B and holds about a quarter of OpenAI.
OpenAI also unveiled 'Pando', a git-repository backend for coding agents, this week.
